cuts.raw_narration: In a dim hospital corridor, Killua, the white-haired boy, walks in with his younger sister Alluka, a dark-haired girl in a pink dress. He crouches to her level and gently asks if she slept well on the way there, then explains that a friend of his is here and is really sick and that he wants to help him feel better. Alluka listens quietly and nods. Killua stands back up, takes her hand, and starts leading her further down the corridor toward Gon's room, making it clear this whole trip is about saving that friend.

Before they go in, Killua kneels down in front of Alluka again and tells her not to worry, that everything is going to be fine. Looking her right in the eyes, he promises they'll always be together from now on. Alluka's expression softens into a small, shining-eyed smile as she takes in the promise, and Killua smiles back at her — a quiet, private moment between the two siblings before he has to ask her, and the entity inside her called Nanika, for the wish that could bring his friend back.

Inside Gon's hospital room, Killua sits close to Alluka and, in a strained voice, begs, "Please, Nanika, please heal my friend Gon." Alluka's face shifts: her eyes and mouth turn into pitch-black hollows and her expression goes eerily blank as Nanika takes over. The switched-in Nanika slowly reaches her small hands out toward the bed where Gon lies, and the room begins to glow, the air around her starting to shimmer with the first stirrings of her power.

That power detonates. A brilliant, waterfall-like curtain of white Nen light pours down over Gon's bed and the medical equipment around him, filling the whole room. Killua sits at Nanika's side, terrified, sweating, his teeth grit as the light washes past him — he knows this is the moment his friend either comes back or doesn't. Far away, across the Hunter Association headquarters, other Hunters freeze mid-conversation, staring at the ceiling and muttering that they've never felt anything like this before as the wave of Nen rolls over them: Nanika is healing Gon, and everyone can feel it.

Cut to the Hunter Association Chairman Election. On the debate stage, Pariston — the smooth blond man in the white striped suit — smiles and asks Leorio, the tall man in the black suit and round glasses standing next to him, what he'll actually do if he becomes chairman. Leorio doesn't hesitate. He leans into the microphone and, glaring straight at Pariston, snarls, "I'm gonna save Gon, and you'll help, whether you like it or not." He jabs his mic toward Pariston, whose polished smile stiffens into something more wary as the whole hall registers that Leorio's entire campaign has one purpose: saving his friend.

In the audience, Cheadle — the green-haired, dog-faced Zodiac in the white coat — has been sitting tensely, clenching her gloved hands in her lap while Pariston works the crowd. She finally stands, raises her hand, and walks up onto the stage to join Leorio and Pariston at the microphones. Facing the hall, she declares that if Leorio is elected chairman, she'll volunteer to be his advisor and personally conduct a comprehensive review of the bylaws and the Hunter exam, even offering to leave the Zodiacs to reassure any voters who are worried about Leorio's inexperience — publicly stacking the Zodiacs' credibility behind him, right in front of Pariston.

Later, with the crowd already dispersing in the background, Cheadle rounds on Pariston and demands to know if that really was all the information he had — that he trusted his entire loss to people he'd never even met, just to save Gon. Pariston, still in his white striped suit, still wearing that unbothered half-smile, calmly answers that he trusts Ging as a worthy enemy, and since these are the very same friends Ging himself trusted to save his son, he trusted them too. He adds, almost cheerfully, that he'd be foolish not to. Cheadle stares at him, hard-eyed, as the manipulator finally admits — with a smile — that he was beaten the moment Gon's friends were let into the game.
